title: First restoration transition
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a state type, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine on input $x$, let $a$ be an action, let $h$ be a finite history list, and let $p$ be an input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions. Starting the restoration machine at the checkpoint for the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$, with history $h$ extended by the entry recording the symbols under the work heads of $c$ and the work-head moves prescribed by $a$, one step gives the intermediate restoration configuration for $c$, $a$, $h$, and $p$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine on input $x$
$h$ is a finite list of history entries for $k$ work tapes
$p$ is a valid input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions
replaced:
Let $c$ be a source configuration, $a$ an action, $h$ a history list, and $p$ an
input-head position. One step of the restoration machine from the checkpoint at
$p$ for the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$, whose history is $h$
extended by the entry recording $a$ (the symbols under the work heads of $c$ and
the head moves of $a$), equals the mid-restoration configuration for $c$, $a$, $h$
and $p$: the recorded head moves are reversed, the overwritten symbols are
retained in finite control, and the cells of that history entry are erased.
